endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: validate de-identification before any dataset is used in AI training or model development

endorsements.title: People process technology and operations framework for establishing AI governance in healthcare organizations
endorsements.quote: To maintain an accurate inventory and visibility of all AI products utilized within the organization, all AI products should be registered with the AI governance committee.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether a required intake and registration process for AI solutions reduces unreviewed use, and no supplied study documents how often AI tools enter use without review. The single endorsement quote addresses validating de-identification before training rather than intake registration, so support for R033 currently rests on expert framework guidance alone.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies of the practice and zero studies of the hazard. The one endorsing source, a CHAI playbook, is framework guidance, and its quoted text concerns de-identification of training data, which is indirect to mandatory intake registration. Under GRADE conventions, this supports no certainty rating for effect.

No supplied study measures how many AI tools reach clinical use without review or what harm follows when they do. Without that baseline, a health system cannot estimate how many errors an intake gate would intercept before they reach patients.

commentary.research_gap: Studies should first measure how often AI tools enter use in health systems without registration or review, and then compare systems with and without mandatory intake processes on unreviewed deployments, time to deployment, staff burden, and downstream safety events.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether an intake requirement is feasible for resource-limited safety-net systems, or whether it changes exposure to unreviewed tools for these patients, remains unknown.
